This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Iran FM warns of "even bigger miscalculation" on Hormuz after Trump claims U.S. has "total control": Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned the United States on Thursday against what he called "an even bigger miscalculation on the Strait of Hormuz," a day after President Donald Trump claimed Washington had "total control" of the waterway. "The U.S. has long miscalculated due to intelligence failures. Case in point: The war on Iran," Araghchi on X. "Worse than fake news is fake intelligence. Be careful." He ended his post: "Allah is Great, Greater than ANY power on Earth. In Allah we trust." Trump on Truth Social on Wednesday that the U.S. had "total control over the Strait of Hormuz," describing the U.S. naval blockade as a "WALL OF STEEL" and claimed "there is nothing Iran can do about it," before concluding his post with: "Praise be to Allah!" Washington Post : U.S. intelligence viewed Israeli warning of Iranian plot to kill Trump as "low confidence": U.S. intelligence officials were skeptical of Israeli intelligence alleging an Iranian plot to assassinate President Donald Trump, with one official describing the warning as "Israeli-derived, not U.S.-generated, and viewed as low confidence," The Washington Post . Despite the doubts, the Secret Service took extraordinary precautions as Trump left a NATO summit in Ankara on July 8, secretly moving him from Air Force One in an airport catering truck to another military aircraft that flew him to Britain under F-16 escort. "The Secret Service has had three near misses with this president, so they're not taking any chances," one official said. Some U.S. intelligence officials, however, believed Israel provided the warning partly to influence U.S. policy, with a former official saying it fit a broader pattern of Israeli intelligence reporting "designed as much to shape presidential decision-making as to inform it." Slight bump in Hormuz traffic: Fourteen vessels through the Strait of Hormuz on August 11, up from twelve on both August 9 and 10, according to data cited by Kpler. Of the 14 crossings, 12 vessels entered the Persian Gulf and only two exited. Iran's Persian Gulf Waterway Management Organization rejected claims by President Trump and U.S. officials that Hormuz was open on Wednesday, saying that the Strait "remains blocked and will not be reopened until Iran's conditions are accepted." Hapag-Lloyd, one of the world's top container shipping companies, reported on Thursday that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to conflict in the Middle East cost the group $600 million in its second quarter. Iran reports oil pollution off Qeshm Island, calls for Hormuz environmental fees: Oil pollution was documented at three coastal sites on Qeshm Island and in surrounding waters, with preliminary evidence pointing to a foreign bulk carrier as the source, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said in a on X Thursday. Baghaei said the incident underscored the need to include environmental protection fees in any future arrangement governing the Strait of Hormuz, arguing that all parties benefiting from shipping through the waterway have a "legal and moral obligation" to address environmental damage. Iran kills two accused of intelligence ties to U.S. and Israel: Iranian forces two members "affiliated with American and Israeli intelligence agencies" during a confrontation in southeastern Iran, the Islamic Republic News Agency reported on Thursday. The Iranian intelligence ministry also announced the arrest of four people accused of planning to destabilize the Sistan and Baluchestan province and damage its infrastructure. Yemen Yemen 's Saudi-backed government claims success against Ansarallah attack: The Yemeni army repelled an Ansarallah attack on positions on the Al‐Mafalis zone in the southeastern province of Taiz in Yemen, an official of the Tor al‐Bahah military axis, an affiliate of the Saudi-backed government. The official claimed that "the terrorist Houthi militias suffered heavy losses." The government side also suffered casualties, with at least one soldier and another critically wounded in the clashes, Yemeni military officials told AP. Saudi tankers reroute around Africa as empty fleet heads toward Gulf: Saudi tanker movements are amid continued shipping risks around the Bab Al-Mandab and Strait of Hormuz, according to researcher Ali (@MerruX). A fleet of Saudi VLCCs is sailing around the Cape of Good Hope, avoiding potential Ansarallah attacks near Bab Al-Mandab, while nearly all Saudi tankers remaining in the Red Sea have reportedly switched off their AIS tracking. More than 12 empty Saudi tankers are reportedly heading toward the Gulf of Oman and UAE ports, potentially preparing to cross Hormuz and load crude. Their entry could replenish the shrinking pool of tankers inside the Gulf as outbound oil flows accelerate. At Bab Al-Mandab, traffic modestly to 40 crossings on August 11, up from 36 on August 9 and 35 on August 10, though normal shipping patterns remain heavily disrupted. Ambrey joins major salvage operation for stricken tanker off Oman: Maritime risk firm Ambrey it is involved in the salvage of the Caroline Bezengi tanker, which was struck near Oman's Hallaniyat Islands in Dhofar, as part of a major international response involving salvage vessels, aircraft, specialist personnel, and more than 100 tons of equipment. Specialists have boarded the tanker with support from the Royal Air Force of Oman to begin stabilizing the vessel and its cargo. An international oil-spill response company has also been contracted. Ambrey said the operation is complicated by extreme weather and sea conditions brought on by the Khareef monsoon. The internationally sanctioned tanker, carrying an estimated 800,000 barrels of Russian oil, ran aground on June 30 near an Omani marine nature reserve that is home to wildlife. The vessel had reported difficulties off Yemen on June 8 following an explosion. No group claimed responsibility for the attack. X suspends Ansarallah spokesperson account: The of Yahya Saree, the spokesperson for Ansarallah, has been suspended. It is unclear what prompted X to take down the account, which had over 121,000 followers, though a notice on the account says, "X suspends accounts which violate the X Rules." For those who want to follow in real time, the spokesperson maintains a presence on . Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, one Palestinian was killed and seven injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,389 killed, with 174,266 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,260 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,154, while 808 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. VIDEO: Ryan Grim discusses Israel's continued violations of the Gaza ceasefire agreement . Israel kills Palestinian child in Gaza City strike: An Israeli in the Beit Lahiya area of Gaza City on Wednesday killed a 10-year-old Palestinian child and wounded several others. Israeli strikes kill two, including Gaza police chief: An Israeli airstrike killed the director of police in the Gaza Governorate, Col. Jamal Abu Kamil, 43, after targeting his vehicle on Al-Rashid Street southwest of Gaza City on Thursday, according to Gaza's Interior Ministry. Separately, a Palestinian was and several others wounded on Thursday in an Israeli drone strike on the Al-Amal neighborhood, west of Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip, WAFA reported. Israel detains Palestinians, destroys homes, and re-establishes settlement in occupied West Bank: Bethlehem: Israeli settlers assaulted a child in Artas on Thursday, violently entering a home near the Solomon's Pools tourist area and brutally beating a 16-year-old. Israeli settlers a farm in Minya, stealing over 100 sheep and uprooting over 100 olive trees, WAFA reported. During the attack, the settlers reportedly attacked two residents of the farm, stole a vehicle and damaged another, and vandalized the house, with Israeli forces detaining three family members. Jenin: Israeli settlers the "Ganim" settlement on Thursday, 21 years after settlers left the area as part of a 2005 disengagement plan, tightening controls in the surrounding area and closing several roads. Defense Minister Israel Katz participated in the ceremony for the settlement's reopening, alongside settler leader Yossi Dagan and members of the Knesset. The move comes days after Israel began demolishing 27 Palestinian buildings in the governorate. Nablus: Israeli authorities the Palestinian families occupying two homes in Qusra, and seized 16 other homes as temporary military barracks, the village's mayor told WAFA on Thursday. A Wednesday statement from the Israeli human rights group B'Tselem the escalations in Qusra, noting that outposts are being used to "force the families out and take over their homes," and said they were "not an isolated incident." Qalqilya: Israeli forces seven Palestinians in Qalqilya on Thursday morning, according to WAFA, all of whom were related to Palestinians recently killed by Israel. Jericho: Israeli settlers around 20 seasonal shelters used by Palestinian migrant farmers near Jericho on Thursday. Hebron: Israeli forces 3 young Palestinian men from Beit Ummar on Thursday, according to WAFA. East Jerusalem: Dozens of Israelis the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem on Thursday, WAFA reported. Hamas says it will participate in Palestinian elections in November: Senior Hamas official Husam Badran Al-Aqsa Radio that the movement has made a "clear decision" to participate in legislative and Palestinian National Council elections in November, calling for clarity about the schedule for elections to replace President Mahmoud Abbas as well. Badran said the group seeks "the largest and broadest possible national coalition" of factions, independents and political blocs. He also rejected attempts to sideline the group, saying that "no one has the right to impose a political condition for participation" in the elections. Lebanon Israeli forces blow up and burn homes in southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire" framework: Israeli forces in Majdal Zoun and Mansouri and the surrounding valleys on Thursday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Israeli forces also explosions in Majdal Zoun and nearby valleys, while an Israeli infantry force was in the area between Aita Al-Jabal and Beit Yahoun in the Bint Jbeil district. Separately, Israeli aircraft struck Mansouri in two waves overnight. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam on Thursday reposted a on X condemning Israel's "systematic destruction" of southern Lebanese villages after the original post was deleted, saying someone had gained access to his account and removed it. Salam condemned Israeli attacks in Mansouri, Zawtar Al-Sharqieh, and Kfartabnit in the post, rejected Israel's claim that it was targeting military facilities, and added that Lebanon's sovereignty and southerners' right to return and rebuild "are not matters open to compromise." Report: Israeli forces are deliberately setting southern Lebanon ablaze: Israel incendiary materials from drones and fired white phosphorus and flares into woodlands nearly every day since the June 17 ceasefire, Civil defense chief Hussein Fakih told The Guardian. He estimated fires have affected 30% to 40% of land near the frontline. Conservationist Hisham Younes called the campaign "ecocide," saying the destruction is making the land uninhabitable. U.S. official says Israel expected to abide by Lebanon framework after Katz vows not to withdraw: The U.S. expects Israel to act in accordance with the framework agreed with Lebanon, a State Department official Asharq, responding to Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz's declaration that Israeli forces would not withdraw from areas they control in Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza. The official said a "permanent military presence in southern Lebanon is inconsistent with the commitments made under the framework," which provides for a conditional, phased Israeli redeployment tied to Hezbollah's disarmament. Katz said Wednesday during a visit to an Israeli military position in southern Lebanon: "We will not move from here and we will not withdraw." Lebanese presidency denies report that Aoun called Hezbollah a "cancer" in meeting with Trump: The Lebanese presidency's media office an Al-Akhbar report, saying the remarks attributed to President Joseph Aoun were "incorrect." The Al-Akhbar report Aoun told Trump that repeated attempts at dialogue with Hezbollah had failed, that the group was now under Iranian leadership, and that Lebanon's Shiites did not support it to the extent it claimed. It also alleged that Aoun described Hezbollah as "the cancer Lebanon is suffering from" that required "complete eradication" rather than dialogue or partial solutions. U.S. News Multiple USS Abraham Lincoln sailors have tried to jump overboard amid extended deployment: Concerns are growing about a mental health crisis and the risk of self-harm aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln as 5,000 sailors and marines are in their ninth month at sea--a record for an aircraft carrier--with worsening conditions onboard, according to reports in the and . Both papers reported thwarted suicide attempts by service members, with multiple attempts by sailors to jump overboard. The USS Abraham Lincoln was sent to the Gulf amid the Iran war and U.S. blockade. Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) sent a to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao on Wednesday demanding to know what action is being taken to improve conditions for sailors onboard. "There have been widespread reports of shortages of basic supplies, water contamination, plumbing issues, deteriorating mental health, deck safety concerns, and disruptions in the mail system," Blumenthal wrote. Rep. Mike Levin of California also military families describing poor conditions onboard, including "Moldy showers, broken toilets, laundry down for weeks, long stretches with no hot water, a meal that came down to half a cup of rice and two tortillas." Third detainee dies after detention at Newark ICE facility: Jose Chajon-Raxon, a Guatemalan immigrant, at a hospital as a result of a "medical emergency," according to a Wednesday Department of Homeland Security statement, making his the third death connected to the Newark facility since it reopened in May 2025. A nurse at the facility reported Chajon-Raxon had a seizure the day after he arrived at the facility, after which he was taken to the hospital, according to the DHS statement. The New Jersey Attorney General's office opened a civil rights investigation into the facility last Friday amid mounting scrutiny over its medical care and conditions. DHS spent $464M on planes for deportations that have mostly sat unused: The Department of Homeland Security $464 million on a no-bid contract last fall to buy ten used airplanes, justified as urgently needed for deportation flights, but has largely left the fleet idle, The New York Times reported on Thursday. Three luxury business jets were loaned or proposed for loan to other agencies, including one leased to the FBI for Director Kash Patel's travel, and seven Boeing 737s parked for months at an airport in Lake Charles, Louisiana. The contract went to Daedalus Aviation Corporation, an Arlington, Virginia firm with no prior federal contracts whose chairman donated to a political committee tied to former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem and separately received a nearly $700 million contract under her leadership. Trump administration awards controversial anti-trafficking group $158M contract for migrant child legal services: The Trump administration Utah-based Our Rescue, formerly known as Operation Underground Railroad, a no-bid $158 million contract to provide legal services to unaccompanied migrant children, according to a Friday notice from the Department of Health and Human Services cited by NPR, though it remains unclear whether the group employs immigration lawyers. Our Rescue was founded by activist Tim Ballard , subject of the 2023 film "Sound of Freedom," who was later quietly removed after facing sexual exploitation accusations he has denied, and is now led by CEO Derek Benner , a former ICE official. Treasury permanently halts shell company ownership reporting requirement : The Treasury Department Tuesday it is permanently halting collection of "beneficial ownership" data about private American companies previously under the 2021 Corporate Transparency Act, a law intended to help law enforcement track shell companies used for money laundering and drug trafficking. Beneficial owners are those who own 25% or more of a reporting company, according to the law. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called it a move to eliminate "a burdensome reporting requirement for millions of law-abiding business owners without compromising our national security." Sen. Elizabeth Warren said the move was "a gift to cartels, criminals and U.S. adversaries" that dismisses law enforcement warnings about the risks of underreporting. Hegseth says "anti-trafficking coalition" will do "bad things to bad people": Hegseth on military leaders from 18 Latin American countries to expand joint operations against drug traffickers at a Panama meeting of the U.S.-led counter-cartel coalition, declaring the group's motto would be "we do bad things to bad people." Hegseth said Honduras and Colombia had agreed to allow joint operations alongside Ecuador and Guatemala, building on a Pentagon campaign that has conducted 66 boat strikes killing at least 221 people. Hegseth claimed at the conference the strikes cut suspected drug vessels by more than half, though a recent Times investigation found cocaine remains as accessible in the U.S. as before the campaign began. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Russian military officer assassinated in Crimea : A Russian military officer was in a bombing in the city of Sevastopol in Russian-annexed Crimea. A Russian woman was arrested and accused of carrying out the assassination on behalf of Ukrainian intelligence services. Russian Telegram channels identified the officer as Robert Shageyev, a former Ukrainian naval commander who reportedly defected to Russia during its 2014 annexation of Crimea. Myrotvorets, an unofficial Ukrainian website that provides a database of people alleged to be as war criminals or traitors, said Shageyev had been "liquidated." Civilian toll in Ukraine in July at highest level since May 2022: The number of civilians killed in Ukraine in July reached its highest level since the first months of the Russian invasion, according to the United Nations. "At least 437 civilians were killed and 2,610 injured in Ukraine in July 2026, a 30% increase compared to June 2026...and a 70% increase compared to July 2025," to the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission. "The number of child casualties (17 killed; 166 injured) was the highest since April 2022." Taiwan throttles internet during anti-blockade drill: Taiwan deliberately slowed mobile internet service across the island's north for 30 minutes on Thursday, testing communications disruptions during a Chinese attack during a raid that included air-raid sirens and police clearing the streets of Taipei. The exercise was part of the 10-day Han Kuang war games, which include military and civil-defense preparations for a potential invasion. Taiwan's navy and coast guard also held their first joint anti-blockade exercise on Wednesday, escorting a simulated merchant vessel to an east-coast port as a minesweeper cleared a navigation channel. Turkey shares details of planned military cooperation under new defense pact: Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia plan to high-level political and military bodies, conduct joint exercises, and expand defense production under the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement signed on August 7, Turkey's defense ministry said. The countries plan exercises involving ground, naval, and air forces, air-defense systems, and drones. They will also pursue joint weapons development and production, focusing on autonomous systems, electronic warfare, and artificial intelligence. Turkey says the pact could expand to include other countries, including Egypt, and is also participating in talks in Jeddah over a proposed international coalition to protect Red Sea shipping. Japan protests Russian official visit to disputed islands: Russian President Vladimir Putin the island of Iturup on Thursday, marking his first trip to the Russian-administered Kuril Islands claimed by Japan. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called the visit "absolutely unacceptable," while Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi summoned Russia's ambassador to lodge a formal protest. The islands have been disputed since the end of World War II when they were occupied by Russian forces who expelled the existing Japanese population and their status has remained contested between Tokyo and Moscow. Australian military whistleblower released on parole: Former Australian military lawyer David McBride was on parole Thursday after serving 27 months for leaking classified defense documents that helped expose alleged war crimes by Australian special forces in Afghanistan. McBride was sentenced in 2024 to five years and eight months in prison after pleading guilty to leaking classified documents and providing them to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation. A subsequent government inquiry found credible evidence that Australian soldiers unlawfully killed 39 Afghans and two former Australian special forces soldiers were charged with war crimes. McBride, who has been diagnosed with treatable lung cancer, will serve the remainder of his sentence under community supervision. RSF appears to retake Kurmuk as drone offensive widens: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces , a strategic town on the Ethiopian border, just one month after the army recaptured it, according to Sudanese analysts and local reports. Reports accused Ethiopia of enabling RSF operations in Blue Nile through drone flights and troop movements through its territory and Reuters had previously uncovered an RSF training camp near Assosa. The army has not confirmed the loss, and the claim has not been independently verified. The apparent capture followed an RSF advance through nearby Geisan, where fighting killed more than 20 civilians Tuesday and displaced roughly 2,500 people, according to UN agencies. On Wednesday, the RSF launched drone attacks on Khartoum, Bahri, Omdurman, Atbara, Ed Damer and el-Obeid, marking its first strikes on the capital since May. Around eight drones hit el-Obeid, killing at least two people and wounding others, Reuters and the UN reported. Emergency Lawyers separately accused an army vehicle of killing five civilians, including women and children, near Jabra al-Sheikh in North Kordofan. Sudan Tribune reported that the SAF thwarted an RSF assault on the area. RSF-appointed Kordofan governor defects, urges fighters to "return to homeland": Hamad Mohammed Hamid, appointed governor of Sudan's Kordofan region last year by the Rapid Support Forces-linked Tasis government, from the RSF in an interview with Al Arabiya. Hamid said the Sudanese people had no choice but to unite against what he called "unruly militias." He accused the RSF of stoking tribal, communal, and racial tensions across the country, and said the Tasis government serves only as a political front for the paramilitary force. Hamid, who was also named to the Tasis presidential council, called for legitimate state institutions to be restored across Kordofan and Darfur. Cholera kills 1,721 people in South Sudan, over 110,000 infected in country 's longest-running outbreak on record: South Sudan is battling its in recorded history, with more than 110,000 cases and 1,721 deaths reported across 55 counties since late September 2025. National Health Minister Luke Thompson Thoan cited poor sanitation, low immunity, and large displaced populations as key drivers of the outbreak. "That is a big number of deaths, and we are doing all we can to stop the epidemic," he said, Health officials are also managing a growing Mpox outbreak that has expanded from Juba to nine counties, with 128 confirmed cases, and are preparing for potential cross-border transmission of Bundibugyo Ebola from the DRC, outlining a $30 million, six-month preparedness plan. | | ---|---|--- 📖 In West Bank Village, a New Israeli Order Enables Settler Attacks While Claiming to Prevent Them 🛒 for your Drop News/Not Bombs Hoodie 💬 our Whatsapp Broadcast Channel for the latest reporting, podcasts, and breaking news, delivered directly ⚠️ You can go to your to unsubscribe from the Drop Site Daily newsletter--while still getting the rest of our reporting Become a Drop Site News Paid Subscriber Drop Site News is reader-supported. Hey folks,
[Jack Cocchiarella](https://open.substack.com/users/112946688-jack-cocchiarella?utm_source=mentions) and I got into everything today--from Stephen Miller's latest immigration cruelty and his increasingly awkward place in Trump's orbit to a much bigger question Democrats need to answer: **Are we actually prepared to use power?**
This one gets funny, angry, personal, and pretty damn blunt. And by the end, we're talking about what accountability really needs to look like if Democrats get another shot at governing.
* [**00:05:09**] Stephen Miller is back in the spotlight--and we dig into the administration's push targeting thousands of unaccompanied immigrant children.
* [**00:11:49**] Is Trump turning on Stephen Miller? We break down the humiliations piling up inside a White House that looks increasingly chaotic.
* [**00:17:16**] The palace intrigue gets messier: Pete Hegseth, Trump's cabinet, and why dysfunction doesn't necessarily mean anyone is getting fired.
* [**00:23:18**] We get into the right's obsession with women, voting rights, and culture-war distractions--and why Democrats need to start shifting the conversation instead of constantly reacting.
* [**00:30:11**] The bigger argument: Democrats need leaders who understand power, demand accountability, and are willing to make genuinely difficult structural changes.

This conversation is about something much bigger than Stephen Miller or the latest chaos inside Trump's White House. It's about power--who has it, who's willing to use it, and whether Democrats are prepared to fight for accountability and rebuild the institutions that are failing us. That's also why independent media matters. We need more places willing to have these conversations, call out corruption, and push back against a right-wing media machine built to dominate the conversation.

I’m suing Donald Trump again.

(If that’s all you need to hear, **[you can support our work holding this lawless administration accountable by contributing right here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137164220/639859896/2110272206?refcode=260813em_rb_bigbanks&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MzlhNDZkOC0yYjk3LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=98XEiwDgPVJhNioui9Nj9Oj_m96B1nF0U9g-2dFJU98=) **— your support makes each and every lawsuit possible.)

Here’s what’s going on right now:

California law requires mortgage lenders (like the big banks) to pay interest on the money they require borrowers to deposit to cover their taxes and insurance.

These laws are designed to prevent the big banks doing the lending from profiting at the borrower’s expense.

Now, the Trump administration — _at the request of banking lobbyists_ — is trying to slash these consumer protections, taking money away from Californians and putting it directly into the pockets of big banks.

This is blatantly illegal, and it will only worsen the effects of the already devastating affordability crisis facing Californians and people all around the country.

**So yet again, I am taking Donald Trump to court, along with nine other attorneys general, to stand up for our state laws that protect consumers from being taken advantage of by big banks.**

---

It's called the suspense file. Here's what it means. | |

Peter - Today is suspense day. Let me explain:

Twice each session, bills with a price tag attached go to the suspense file. In one hearing, the Appropriations Committee reads a list: bills that are named move forward; bills that don't, die. Without a vote, debate, or explanation. It happens fast.

Today, several of my bills are on that list: My **No Kings Act** , the first bill in the country that would allow people to hold ICE accountable for violating their constitutional rights.

A bill to **legalize plug-in solar** , so any renter can cut their own power bill.

The **Science Bond** , to put $12 billion into research California can't count on Washington to fund anymore.

A bill to **stop insurance companies from denying you care** your doctor says you need.

On November 8th, 2016, millions of Pennsylvanians made their way to the polls on Election Day. At the top of the ballot was the Presidential election — an election Donald Trump won by less than one percentage point.
But as Pennsylvanians filled out the rest of their ballot, they eventually stumbled across my name. I was running for Attorney General — my first ever statewide election.
And later that night? We won, Derek. On the same night Trump won Pennsylvania, Democrats won the Attorney General’s office.

| | Peter — I’ve met some characters, but this one takes the cake...

_My opponent believes in some things that would make your mama blush. _

My opponent has decided the United States _“has been lost” _because President Trump is somehow running the country _“as if he was its dictator.”_

* _They support legalizing prostitution._
* _They are pro-choice._
* _They oppose Education Freedom Accounts that give Arkansas families real choices for their children._
* _And they want to abolish Social Security._

Legalizing prostitution? Abolishing Social Security? Declaring America “lost” over a president they don’t like?

Folks, this isn’t a platform. **It’s a cautionary tale with a campaign logo.**

Let me tell you why this election matters: = Donald Trump refuses to let go of his 2020 loss, and his administration is officially coming after Arizona to relitigate the presidential election. This move to subpoena Arizona for voting records comes after the FBI raided an elections office in another swing state, and as Trump continues to push conspiracy theories about voter fraud that cost him the 2020 race. = Why is Trump doing this? So he can justify rolling back our voting rights and giving the federal government more power over elections. This is exactly why this year’s gubernatorial election is so critical: I’m being challenged by Andy Biggs, a Trump-backed MAGA congressman who voted against certifying the 2020 election results and was reportedly involved in planning the Jan. 6 insurrection. If Biggs wins this toss-up seat, there’s no telling what he’ll do in 2028, but he already has a record of putting Trump before Arizonans and the Constitution. name: Deb Haaland
subject: Do you believe in my vision for New Mexico? Add your name!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5298?refcode=jtk1196-su-nd&t=1&akid=11664%2E400544%2E_MTzRx)
---
Friend: In a moment, I'm going to share with you my vision for New Mexico — **_[but first, can I ask you to take 30 seconds to personally endorse my campaign for Governor?](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202608_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk1196-su-nd&refcode=jtk1196-su-nd&t=2&akid=11664%2E400544%2E_MTzRx)_**
| | [Add My Name](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202608_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk1196-su-nd&refcode=jtk1196-su-nd&t=3&akid=11664%2E400544%2E_MTzRx)
---
This message is a bit on the longer side, but because you're invested in the future of New Mexico, I hope you'll take the time to read my plan. **As New Mexico’s next Governor, I will:**
**Build Education That Works for New Mexico by:**
* Ensuring students can read before third grade by identifying literacy challenges early and providing targeted support when children fall behind

* Strengthening early literacy screening, expanding bilingual and reading instruction, and investing in summer reading and after-school programs that reinforce learning beyond the school day

* Bolstering access to universal childcare, because learning begins long before a child enters a classroom

* Directing unspent dollars from the Public School Capital Outlay Fund to modernize and improve school facilities so kids can focus on learning

* Expanding outdoor and place-based learning through my Every Child Outdoor Initiative, giving schools the tools and resources to connect classroom instruction to real-world learning that improves engagement and outcomes

**Support New Mexico Families by:**
* Raising the minimum wage and eliminating predatory junk fees

* Passing Paid Family and Medical Leave so people don’t have to choose between caring for their family and making ends meet

* Increasing the child tax credit to put money back into your pockets

* Creating a statewide tenant bill of rights to make renting more affordable and more transparent

* Creating a Critical Sector Housing Fund for workers in critical sectors — like healthcare, behavioral health, social work, education, and more — to recruit more professionals to New Mexico to address endemic shortages that hold our people back

* Aggressively building more housing, eliminating unnecessary red tape, driving state investment into housing, and shortening the time it takes to build a home — and ensuring those homes are built with New Mexican labor

**Back Small Businesses by:**
* Establishing a permanent Office of Small Business to coordinate development programs, fill gaps left by federal cuts, and provide clear access to grants, capital, and state resources

* Cracking down on predatory lending by requiring full transparency in small-business loan disclosures

* Establishing a New Mexico Economic Growth Trust Fund to stabilize our economy in the face of federal uncertainty

**Fix Our Broken Healthcare System by:**
* Protecting and expanding access to healthcare in every part of New Mexico

* Banning medical debt from being included on credit reports

* Expanding New Mexico’s Health Care Affordability Fund to protect access for those who rely on the state marketplace

* Using budget surpluses to fill Medicaid gaps and hire more guides to help people enroll in and keep their benefits

* Ensuring sustainable funding for rural hospitals and clinics, expanding mobile health clinics, and significantly increasing access to outpatient behavioral and mental health care, including a full-scale effort to deliver mental health and homelessness assistance statewide

**Strengthen Public Safety by:**
* Ensuring that law enforcement has the tools, staffing, and technology they need to do their jobs effectively

* Investing in mental and behavioral healthcare and housing stability

* Expanding violence intervention and prevention programs in schools and communities, building accountability systems that emphasize fairness and trust, and investing in community policing models that supplement traditional police work

* Creating a statewide Department of Community Safety staffed with social workers and counselors so law enforcement can focus on violent crime while people get the help they need

* Requiring ICE agents to clearly identify themselves and prohibiting masks that shield misconduct from accountability

New Mexico deserves steady leadership that’s ready on day one, leadership rooted in firsthand knowledge and experience. But the only way we'll be able to make this vision a reality is with strong grassroots support from people like you.
**I'm aiming to get 10,000 endorsements for my campaign before my midnight deadline to show the grassroots strength behind my vision for New Mexico, and I want you to be one of them._[Will you please take a quick moment to sign on now?](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202608_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk1196-su-nd&refcode=jtk1196-su-nd&t=4&akid=11664%2E400544%2E_MTzRx)_**

Thank you for your support,

Deb

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137169403/639878331/-816387931?amount=5&refcode=8.13.26_rs_fr_mm1headshot&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODY2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZTgxYmI5MC0zMjk3LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RUHOnTCx15XIQQ3F6woH-MbMsa6TQIvLASG9FBrWkrA=) Hey Peter, it’s Paige. I wanted to share a little about who I am to show you how I plan on reforming Congress the same way I reformed Scranton as mayor. I started on the Scranton School Board, then worked in the Auditor General’s office digging up waste and fixing nursing home safety. Then, I ran for mayor as an Independent and became the first female mayor of Scranton while eight months pregnant. I’ve been reelected twice since then, because people here believe in the simple idea that government should work as hard as the people it serves. As mayor, I cut red tape, balanced budgets, and led Scranton out of 30 years of financial distress. We delivered more than $155 million in grants, helped build thousands of homes, brought in hundreds of new businesses, and made our streets safer. | | Dear Friend, Wes Moore and his hyperscale Data Center lobbyist allies want Marylanders to believe the race is already decided.

But look beyond the fake headline. His own biased poll shows we will win.

[](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=679c8c509b&e=5bb5efcda7)

name: Aaron Day
subject: I fired the lawyers. Hired AI. Won.
body:
# THE AARON DAY SHOW
Defending Free Will in the Age of Technocracy
S3E33 • Aug 13
## S3E33: I Beat the Attorney General in Federal Court. No Lawyers. My Legal Team Was AI.
[ ](https://daylightfreedom.us22.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2ed19bcf5e9d5b7527326676a&id=5b7cca4518&e=938a87a89b)
The New Hampshire Attorney General's office tried to keep me off the US Senate ballot.
They had the full weight of the State. Career prosecutors. Unlimited resources.
I had a laptop.
No lawyers. No law firm. My legal team was AI.
And tonight, I'm going to walk you through exactly how a federal magistrate judge just issued a Report & Recommendation that the Secretary of State be ordered to accept my Declaration of Intent and put me on the ballot.
The State gets 7 days to object. Certification is August 26. The Secretary of State's deadline is September 2. This is not theoretical. This is docket reality.
But here's why this matters far beyond my Senate race:
If one guy with a laptop and AI can beat the AG's office pro se, the entire gatekeeping racket the two-party duopoly relies on to keep challengers off ballots just cracked open. That's the real story. Not the win. The rigging that tried to stop it.
Tonight I'll show you:
\- Exactly how the AI legal workflow worked (including the cite-verifier that caught the State citing the wrong statute)
\- The precise language of the Report & Recommendation and what the 7-day objection window means
\- The Four Demands I'm putting on Trump, each paired with his own promise on tape
\- Why the September 2 deadline is a pressure point every freedom candidate in America should be watching
This isn't a victory lap. It's a blueprint.
8:00 PM ET. Live. Tonight.
[ Watch Live Aug 13 ](https://daylightfreedom.us22.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2ed19bcf5e9d5b7527326676a&id=8ba1fb2347&e=938a87a89b)

The bridge linking Bandar Abbas and Kehuristan, destroyed in a U.S. strike, is seen in Iran's Hormozgan province on July 19, 2026. Photo by Amir Hossein Khorgooei/Anadolu via Getty Images.
AHVAZ, Iran--When U.S. missiles struck the harbor outside in the port city of Badar Abbas last month, Sajjad saw his livelihood literally go up in smoke.
The small wooden fishing boat that had supported the 56-year-old and his family for years was reduced to a charred husk, along with dozens of other boats lining the docks. Sajjad told Drop Site News that nearly every fisherman he knows lost a vessel that night. Replacing a single boat now costs around 2 billion tomans (around $1,050)--far beyond what most families can afford.
"Both my children are in university," Sajjad said. "Everything depended on that boat. Soon, I may not even be able to pay their tuition."
When U.S. strikes resumed in early July following a two-month pause, the attacks focused heavily on southern Iran. Interviews with residents in hard-hit southern provinces like Khuzestan, Hormozgan, Sistan, and Baluchestan describe strikes not only on military facilities, but also on critical civilian infrastructure, including fishing ports, bridges, telecommunications networks, power plants, hospitals, and transportation corridors.
Dozens of communications towers have been knocked offline in repeated attacks, disrupting internet and telephone services. One attack on a transmission tower near Tappeh Aluakbar in Bandar Abbas killed five people, including a woman who died shielding her son with her body, local residents told Drop Site.
Transportation infrastructure has sustained similar damage. Alireza, a resident of Hormozgan who studies screenwriting and is carefully tracking recent events in the hopes of making a documentary about the war, described strikes on Tappeh Aluakbar overlooking Bandar Abbas, bridges linking Bandar Abbas to Khamir and Rudan, railway infrastructure, and key transportation routes connecting the province. At one destroyed crossing, road crews carved a temporary dirt route through a dry riverbed within hours simply to keep vehicles moving.
The damage extends to the sea as well: Alireza estimates that roughly 300 civilian fishing boats have been destroyed across Bandar Abbas, Bandar Lengeh, Sirik, and Jask, affecting the livelihoods of thousands of people. Two maritime search-and-rescue vessels operating near Bandar Abbas, Qeshm, and Hormuz Island were also put out of service.
Kharg Island, Iran's principal oil export terminal, has long featured in discussions among U.S. officials and defense analysts as a strategically significant site and was bombed in March during the U.S.-Israeli aerial campaign. According to an Iranian military analyst who spoke to Drop Site on condition of anonymity for security reasons, if the U.S. ever sent ground troops to take over the island, Iran's ability to reinforce Kharg would depend heavily on the transportation networks running through Hormozgan.
"They're not simply destroying roads," the analyst said. "They're reducing Iran's ability to move personnel, equipment, and supplies before any future operation ever begins."
Residents and medical workers in Khuzestan also describe the toll on civilians caused by the bombing campaign, particularly children.
Just after midnight on July 15, explosions shook the area surrounding Shahid Baghaei Hospital in Ahvaz, one of southwestern Iran's principal treatment centers for children with cancer and blood disorders. While the hospital was not destroyed in the attack, the blast forced the emergency evacuation of 211 pediatric patients, including children undergoing chemotherapy and several dependent on ventilators.
Hassan, a doctor who works at one of the hospitals where patients were transferred to, said the attack revived memories of the war's opening day in February, when a missile strike on Minab Elementary School killed more than 150 people, most of them children.
"The memory of Minab came back to us immediately," he said. "When we heard the explosion, everyone feared the hospital had been hit."
The children were physically unharmed, but emotionally distraught. "We tried to reassure them," Hassan told Drop Site. "We kept telling them nothing had happened. But children understand more than adults sometimes think. They knew the strike happened next to the hospital, and they were terrified." Many had already lived through the 12-day war the previous year. That trauma, doctors say, will not disappear when this fighting ends.
"This isn't something that simply goes away after the war," Hassan said. "These children will carry it with them."
Razieh, whose apartment overlooks the neighborhood of the hospital, ran outside after hearing the blast and saw smoke rising into the night sky. Since that night, she said, her three-year-old daughter can barely sleep.
"She wakes up even on nights when there isn't any bombing," Razieh said. "She tells me, 'Mom, we're being attacked. I hear bombs.' At some point I couldn't keep pretending nothing had happened."
Hadis, another mother in the same neighborhood, described a similar pattern. Too scared to sleep, her children remain awake until the early hours of the morning. Loud sounds trigger panic. Some refuse to sleep unless a parent lies beside them.
Across parts of Hormozgan, repeated strikes on electricity and communications infrastructure have interrupted power, internet, and phone service during the hottest weeks of the year when daytime temperatures frequently approach 50 degrees Celsius (122 Fahrenheit). The prolonged outages also cause water pumps to stop operating and refrigeration to fail.
"The pattern documented across these accounts touches on core protections under international humanitarian law," said Mohamed Habibi, a human rights lawyer who holds a master's degree in international law from Imam Sadiq University. "The Geneva Conventions and their Additional Protocol I require that attacks distinguish between military and civilian objects, and that any incidental harm to civilians remain proportionate to the concrete military advantage sought. Article 54 of Protocol I explicitly prohibits attacks on objects indispensable to the survival of the civilian population, including water and power infrastructure--a threshold that Hormozgan residents say has already been crossed amid summer temperatures exceeding 50 degrees Celsius."
A second military analyst, who also spoke on condition of anonymity, said the repeated strikes on electricity, communications, and transportation infrastructure appear designed to exacerbate the civilian cost of the conflict.
"In this climate, electricity is part of basic survival," he told Drop Site. "If you remove power, communications, and water at the same time, you're putting enormous pressure on civilian society. The calculation seems to be that if enough pressure is placed on everyday life, people eventually become exhausted and begin questioning whether continued resistance is worth the cost."
Even at military sites,**** the targets appeared designed to maximize casualties rather than just weaken military capabilities.
Shortly after 12:30 a.m. on July 15, residents near the Iranian Army garrison in Bampur, in the Sistan and Baluchestan Province, were awakened by two powerful explosions. Jalalzehi, who lives near the base, rushed outside to find smoke rising above the compound and the surrounding area dark.
By morning, the Army confirmed at least seven soldiers had been killed, including a conscript with fewer than forty days left in his mandatory service. Iranian media reported that thirteen missiles struck the garrison, hitting a dormitory, a guesthouse, and guard posts.
"Military installations such as the Bampur garrison remain lawful targets," Habibi said. "However, the decision to repeatedly strike sleeping quarters rather than command posts or weapons depots raises a separate question long debated among legal scholars: whether maximizing casualties, rather than degrading military capability, played a role in the targeting."
The second military analyst also raised similar questions. "If the objective is simply to reduce a garrison's operational capability, barracks are not the most decisive target," he said. "A strike on command facilities, communications, or weapons depots would have a more direct military effect. Concentrating repeated strikes on dormitories suggests that maximizing casualties may also have been part of the calculation."
Eight days later, on July 23, missiles struck the Shalamcheh border crossing connecting Khuzestan Province with Iraq, as thousands of pilgrims prepared to travel to Karbala for Arbaeen, one of the largest annual religious gatherings in the Shiite calendar. Local residents reported two people killed and eleven wounded, with additional strikes hitting nearby towns.
Hassan, an Iranian pilgrim present during the attack, has crossed the border to make the religious pilgrimage every year for the past decade. Normally, he said, the route is filled with _mokabs_ --volunteer stations providing food, water and medical assistance free of charge to pilgrims making the journey.
"When the missiles hit, people screamed," he recalled. "But no one ran." Instead, men moved toward the perimeter while women and other pilgrims formed lines to carry the wounded until ambulances arrived. "It showed something about our society," Hassan said. "People were frightened, but they chose to help each other before thinking about themselves."

Photo by Amir Hossein Khorgooei/Anadolu via Getty Images. AHVAZ, Iran--When U.S. missiles struck the harbor outside in the port city of Badar Abbas last month, Sajjad saw his livelihood literally go up in smoke. The small wooden fishing boat that had supported the 56-year-old and his family for years was reduced to a charred husk, along with dozens of other boats lining the docks. Sajjad told Drop Site News that nearly every fisherman he knows lost a vessel that night. Replacing a single boat now costs around 2 billion tomans (around $1,050)--far beyond what most families can afford. "Both my children are in university," Sajjad said. "Everything depended on that boat. Soon, I may not even be able to pay their tuition." When U.S. strikes resumed in early July following a two-month pause, the attacks focused heavily on southern Iran. Interviews with residents in hard-hit southern provinces like Khuzestan, Hormozgan, Sistan, and Baluchestan describe strikes not only on military facilities, but also on critical civilian infrastructure, including fishing ports, bridges, telecommunications networks, power plants, hospitals, and transportation corridors. Dozens of communications towers have been knocked offline in repeated attacks, disrupting internet and telephone services. One attack on a transmission tower near Tappeh Aluakbar in Bandar Abbas killed five people, including a woman who died shielding her son with her body, local residents told Drop Site. Transportation infrastructure has sustained similar damage. Alireza, a resident of Hormozgan who studies screenwriting and is carefully tracking recent events in the hopes of making a documentary about the war, described strikes on Tappeh Aluakbar overlooking Bandar Abbas, bridges linking Bandar Abbas to Khamir and Rudan, railway infrastructure, and key transportation routes connecting the province. At one destroyed crossing, road crews carved a temporary dirt route through a dry riverbed within hours simply to keep vehicles moving. The damage extends to the sea as well: Alireza estimates that roughly 300 civilian fishing boats have been destroyed across Bandar Abbas, Bandar Lengeh, Sirik, and Jask, affecting the livelihoods of thousands of people. Two maritime search-and-rescue vessels operating near Bandar Abbas, Qeshm, and Hormuz Island were also put out of service. Kharg Island, Iran's principal oil export terminal, has long featured in discussions among U.S. officials and defense analysts as a strategically significant site and was bombed in March during the U.S.-Israeli aerial campaign. According to an Iranian military analyst who spoke to Drop Site on condition of anonymity for security reasons, if the U.S. ever sent ground troops to take over the island, Iran's ability to reinforce Kharg would depend heavily on the transportation networks running through Hormozgan. "They're not simply destroying roads," the analyst said. "They're reducing Iran's ability to move personnel, equipment, and supplies before any future operation ever begins." Residents and medical workers in Khuzestan also describe the toll on civilians caused by the bombing campaign, particularly children. Just after midnight on July 15, explosions shook the area surrounding Shahid Baghaei Hospital in Ahvaz, one of southwestern Iran's principal treatment centers for children with cancer and blood disorders. While the hospital was not destroyed in the attack, the blast forced the emergency evacuation of 211 pediatric patients, including children undergoing chemotherapy and several dependent on ventilators. Hassan, a doctor who works at one of the hospitals where patients were transferred to, said the attack revived memories of the war's opening day in February, when a missile strike on Minab Elementary School killed more than 150 people, most of them children. "The memory of Minab came back to us immediately," he said. "When we heard the explosion, everyone feared the hospital had been hit." The children were physically unharmed, but emotionally distraught. "We tried to reassure them," Hassan told Drop Site. "We kept telling them nothing had happened. But children understand more than adults sometimes think. They knew the strike happened next to the hospital, and they were terrified." Many had already lived through the 12-day war the previous year. That trauma, doctors say, will not disappear when this fighting ends. "This isn't something that simply goes away after the war," Hassan said. "These children will carry it with them." Razieh, whose apartment overlooks the neighborhood of the hospital, ran outside after hearing the blast and saw smoke rising into the night sky. Since that night, she said, her three-year-old daughter can barely sleep. "She wakes up even on nights when there isn't any bombing," Razieh said. "She tells me, 'Mom, we're being attacked. I hear bombs.' At some point I couldn't keep pretending nothing had happened." Hadis, another mother in the same neighborhood, described a similar pattern. Too scared to sleep, her children remain awake until the early hours of the morning. Loud sounds trigger panic. Some refuse to sleep unless a parent lies beside them. Across parts of Hormozgan, repeated strikes on electricity and communications infrastructure have interrupted power, internet, and phone service during the hottest weeks of the year when daytime temperatures frequently approach 50 degrees Celsius (122 Fahrenheit). The prolonged outages also cause water pumps to stop operating and refrigeration to fail. "The pattern documented across these accounts touches on core protections under international humanitarian law," said Mohamed Habibi, a human rights lawyer who holds a master's degree in international law from Imam Sadiq University. "The Geneva Conventions and their Additional Protocol I require that attacks distinguish between military and civilian objects, and that any incidental harm to civilians remain proportionate to the concrete military advantage sought. Article 54 of Protocol I explicitly prohibits attacks on objects indispensable to the survival of the civilian population, including water and power infrastructure--a threshold that Hormozgan residents say has already been crossed amid summer temperatures exceeding 50 degrees Celsius." A second military analyst, who also spoke on condition of anonymity, said the repeated strikes on electricity, communications, and transportation infrastructure appear designed to exacerbate the civilian cost of the conflict. "In this climate, electricity is part of basic survival," he told Drop Site. "If you remove power, communications, and water at the same time, you're putting enormous pressure on civilian society. The calculation seems to be that if enough pressure is placed on everyday life, people eventually become exhausted and begin questioning whether continued resistance is worth the cost." Even at military sites,** the targets appeared designed to maximize casualties rather than just weaken military capabilities. Shortly after 12:30 a.m. on July 15, residents near the Iranian Army garrison in Bampur, in the Sistan and Baluchestan Province, were awakened by two powerful explosions. Jalalzehi, who lives near the base, rushed outside to find smoke rising above the compound and the surrounding area dark. By morning, the Army confirmed at least seven soldiers had been killed, including a conscript with fewer than forty days left in his mandatory service. Iranian media reported that thirteen missiles struck the garrison, hitting a dormitory, a guesthouse, and guard posts. "Military installations such as the Bampur garrison remain lawful targets," Habibi said. "However, the decision to repeatedly strike sleeping quarters rather than command posts or weapons depots raises a separate question long debated among legal scholars: whether maximizing casualties, rather than degrading military capability, played a role in the targeting." The second military analyst also raised similar questions. "If the objective is simply to reduce a garrison's operational capability, barracks are not the most decisive target," he said. "A strike on command facilities, communications, or weapons depots would have a more direct military effect. Concentrating repeated strikes on dormitories suggests that maximizing casualties may also have been part of the calculation." Eight days later, on July 23, missiles struck the Shalamcheh border crossing connecting Khuzestan Province with Iraq, as thousands of pilgrims prepared to travel to Karbala for Arbaeen, one of the largest annual religious gatherings in the Shiite calendar. Local residents reported two people killed and eleven wounded, with additional strikes hitting nearby towns. Hassan, an Iranian pilgrim present during the attack, has crossed the border to make the religious pilgrimage every year for the past decade. Normally, he said, the route is filled with mokabs --volunteer stations providing food, water and medical assistance free of charge to pilgrims making the journey. "When the missiles hit, people screamed," he recalled. "But no one ran." Instead, men moved toward the perimeter while women and other pilgrims formed lines to carry the wounded until ambulances arrived. "It showed something about our society," Hassan said. "People were frightened, but they chose to help each other before thinking about themselves." All residents asked to be referred to by their first names only for security reasons. name: Senator Debra Altschiller
subject: I'm endorsing Carleigh Beriont
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Carleigh Beriont for Congress
body:
Carleigh is a principled hard worker who gets things done

| |
---
| | [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/MTFfg2SruSULJtnzc9zOhQ~~/AAUS1hA~/4fLoc43lp7z3X-v-rwme8vmtXpOXT9oA11J7BS7_gIksuICsuEh5F4guRmBDulSWrPBX6kT7EhOKgdslDjazUqgDnSXr66sRh1Juwk3vb5f10LESeq72W7gNKwMqKozQTi5Xl7zW9q4uTVbr2fOBLccKqCevH5Q0dzN8YG__LB22DgeBDI2HbkuMNS2nPP67KK6VmfJQIo4DXAf_iYvhM8vqHLX4ZhHW-ZHWWsnBSnnF5O_TgC0pypJ5rNAV1ms3QpT5uj7C72GqzymC9327Hw~~) Dear David, Some people just shine and inspire people around them to rise to the occasion. Carleigh Beriont shines. She shines light on the dark places where elderly people are threatened with not being able to age in the hometowns they love and have contributed to. She shines light on where children are hungry for lunch and great public schools are in need. She shines light on places where workers need fair wages, good health insurance and a social security system that will be ready for them when they take off their work shoes for good. Carleigh Beriont advocated alongside me for strict regulations on data centers, an issue of growing concern across the nation. As primary sponsor of Senate Bill 439, I fought to establish critical common-sense regulations for data center development — which were then gutted by Republican amendments. The result was not a framework; it was an abdication of responsibility. Beriont also recognizes the threat to our energy grid, our drinking water and quality of life if AI data centers are allowed to proliferate in the Granite State. She advocated for this bill, telling the Union Leader, “Once again, Republicans in our state government put Big Tech ahead of the health and welfare of New Hampshire residents.” She fought against the Republicans' hijacking of this bill to instead recommend a policy that would infringe on community control, essentially eliminating the ability of local government to regulate data center construction and all the issues they bring with them — massive energy and water use, chronic noise and light pollution, and hyperscale footprints that can infringe on neighborhoods and destroy community character. **I’m supporting Carleigh Beriont.** She and her campaign have built an impressive and super-engaged grassroots network of community activists because she is one too. Carleigh is the chair of the Hampton Select Board because she is respected for the way she solves problems. Hampton is one of the measurably most purple towns in the state of New Hampshire. She knows that no one in Congress can work in a vacuum. I respect that Carleigh has run in very contested races and built broad coalitions along the way. She's never walked into an elected position on name recognition alone; she worked for it. Unlike other candidates, Carleigh didn't have to decide if she wanted to run a campaign from her second or third home after swooping in from out of state; she has roots here. I respect the name she has made for herself, the funds she has raised herself and the work she has done for the community. She is the same person on the campaign trail that she is in Select Board meetings and behind closed doors. She is solid. She keeps her fights on policy, not personality. She lifts others up; that is exactly the kind of person we want in Congress representing New Hampshire. Beriont is not waiting until she gets to Washington to take action. Along with speaking out on data center regulation and other important issues, as chair of the Hampton Select Board, she has brought members together for unanimous votes on a number of critical issues. She also fully supported rejecting cooperation with ICE in the town of Hampton. For many months, she has also been at the forefront of the effort to call for a federal investigation of the state-run New Hampshire Youth Development Center. Beriont is a principled hard worker already rolling up her sleeves to get things done. Her truly grassroots campaign reminds me of our former congresswoman from Rochester, feisty and tenacious. **[I’ve watched her campaign catch fire and hope you will join me in supporting Carleigh Beriont for Congress, District 1 by making a donation today.](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/MTFfg2SruSULJtnzc9zOhQ~~/AAUS1hA~/4fLoc43lp7z3X-v-rwme8vmtXpOXT9oA11J7BS7_gIksuICsuEh5F4guRmBDulSWrPBX6kT7EhOKgdslDjazUqgDnSXr66sRh1Juwk3vb5f10LESeq72W7gNKwMqKozQTi5Xl7zW9q4uTVbr2fOBLccKqCevH5Q0dzN8YG__LB22DgeBDI2HbkuMNS2nPP67KK6VmfJQIo4DXAf_iYvhM8vqHLX4ZhHW-ZHWWsnBSnnF5O_TgC0pypJ5rNAV1ms3QpT5uj7C72GqzymC9327Hw~~)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ **** | | [DONATE $10 »](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/kBm1wdkL5SF7_2RWFBamaA~~/AAUS1hA~/K9Gh7MWRq84oUrSLJyGIdlAShpQ7_b0p8fzkOeLbH06mtLMFyoHlzn-SR39QC8_HTTeDEIyUFYELR-_Wnd173CNydKioqtdAkAMyLwSeqMk74Oi5NIADUhmBgrWa8iouCkSTANIfUWGFOuQRSUHGe5k7v0QNMNerwf2dBRWORATfT0yQg6kFSduDWSjfo00Y9TnisQZS2MD6uJ0WHVrjI-LSzpK8weRn4X9QU6M1Z89TI6IFxd_LJJ1kWZ-rmjj7yPpK2qggB9pox0VeXsei_EPsYtbztpqOBDuHNujda7M~)

Friend, We've often compared this campaign to the story of _David and Goliath_. When David faced the notorious giant, everyone told him he was outmatched, _that he had no chance_. They urged him to suit up with a _heavy_ sword and _bulky_ armor, but David knew he had to face Goliath his way. We face a similar giant, today. Marsha Blackburn is _propped up by billionaires and corporate interests._ She thinks everyday people are no match for their money and power. From _way up high in her ivory tower,_ she just can't see the movement that we are building across Tennessee. She’s betting on Tennesseans staying quiet, staying home, and accepting that this is _"just how things are."_ If that’s what she thinks, _she must not be from Tennessee._
### **Every Giant Looks Unbeatable, Until They Fall**
This campaign _isn't built on corporate cash_ or _closed-door photo-op fundraisers._ _**We don't take a single dime of corporate PAC money**_. If you end up going to the polls, you can simply bring your mail ballot with you and the poll workers will dispose of it for you. There is no downside to having the option. Click the button below to request yours today it takes 1 minute REQUEST MAIL BALLOT HERE [] This primary matters. # [Short sellers flee as SpaceX races back to $150](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0c0039-8e17-4934-907e-bf968fe57abd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SpaceX **[shares jumped 11% Wednesday to around $148,](https://substack.com/redirect/ff2ae0c0-22c0-45ae-b1ac-652a7442ddc2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** rebounding more than 40% from the Aug. 3 low near $105 and testing the $150 opening trade **[as short interest collapsed.](https://substack.com/redirect/fe85b7d4-00c9-4b84-95c8-669e9beed982?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0c0039-8e17-4934-907e-bf968fe57abd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Short interest falls sharply:** Short interest fell to about 11% of publicly traded shares from a peak of 34% last week according to S3 Partners. "Shorts that wanted to short are out of bullets," said Ihor Dusaniwsky.
* **Lockup expiration expands float:** Just over 911 million shares became eligible last Thursday after the initial lockup expired, exceeding the 639 million sold in the IPO and representing roughly 7% of outstanding shares.
* **Earnings report sparks sell-off:** The stock initially tumbled after the first earnings disclosed capital expenditures more than twice revenue, drawing short sellers to the limited public float before the rebound.

* **Landside capacity strained:** Underinvestment in landside infrastructure for the last 15 years combined with volume growth is stretching limitations of ports, roads, rail and trucking in many markets.
* **Earnings beat expectations:** Maersk reported preliminary second-quarter underlying EBITDA of $3 billion, well above the $2.04 billion expected by analysts, and raised its 2026 earnings guidance.
* **Hapag reports strength:** Hapag-Lloyd CEO Rolf Habben Jansen said volumes were remarkably strong with a more reasonable supply-demand balance, though Asian hubs like Shanghai struggle with demand.

# [Pandora goes all-in on platinum as silver prices crash](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0c0039-8e17-4934-907e-bf968fe57abd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Pandora is **[continuing its shift toward platinum-plated jewelry to cut exposure to volatile silver prices](https://substack.com/redirect/e78769ba-26ed-4146-8a29-ee243d065855?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** even after silver retreated from multi-year highs, CEO Berta de Pablos-Barbier told CNBC on Thursday.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0c0039-8e17-4934-907e-bf968fe57abd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Portfolio diversification continues:** The world's largest jeweler is replacing some sterling-silver pieces with platinum-plated alternatives to create a more flexible offering of materials for consumers, the CEO said.
* **Silver prices have fallen:** Spot silver traded just under $65 an ounce on Thursday after peaking above $120 in January and standing near $80 when the platinum move was first announced.
* **Guidance and profits rise:** Pandora hiked 2026 organic growth guidance to 0% to 3% from negative 1% to 2% and posted second-quarter operating profit of 1.46 billion Danish crowns with a 20.3% margin.
* **Hedging and stock rebound:** The company has hedged 90-100% of 2027 silver at around $65 while shares rebounded 55% over three months and rose 4% after the better-than-expected results.

# [Cheesecake Factory is leading a massive sector rotation](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0c0039-8e17-4934-907e-bf968fe57abd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Established chains **[including Cheesecake Factory gained roughly 62% at the median over 60 trading days](https://substack.com/redirect/935ba49e-de35-4eb0-85c7-8f5cd6f8adab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while growth names like Chipotle stagnated, creating a gap wider than any from 2016 through 2025.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0c0039-8e17-4934-907e-bf968fe57abd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Median gains hit 62%:** Darden, Texas Roadhouse, Brinker, Cheesecake Factory and BJ's Restaurants rose about 62% at the median over three months as Chipotle, Wingstop and Shake Shack went essentially nowhere.
* **Record gap established:** The divide reached a record 66 points on Aug. 7, topping the previous high of 50 points set in November 2019 according to the Yahoo Finance data.
* **Fundamentals favor sit-downs:** Established group showed 3.3% same-store sales versus 2.3% for growth chains, with forward P/E of 22x versus 35x and stronger recent EPS revisions.
* **Traffic drives winners:** Cheesecake Factory posted 5.8% comparable-sales growth including 2.7% traffic while BJ's rose 6.5% in comps with traffic jumping 8.3% last quarter.

# [Why smart money is hunting Bugatti Veyrons now](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0c0039-8e17-4934-907e-bf968fe57abd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Bugatti Veyron values are rising after years of stagnation, with Hagerty data showing **[roughly 20% gains since 2021 and the earliest cars up 29% to an average of about $1.9 million](https://substack.com/redirect/10612898-5737-4a9a-a5bd-147aad7007fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as younger collectors enter.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0c0039-8e17-4934-907e-bf968fe57abd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Values climb steadily:** Since 2021 Hagerty data shows Veyrons gained roughly 20% overall while the earliest cars are up 29% to an average of about $1.9 million amid shifting collector tastes.
* **Younger buyers emerge:** Buyers chasing Veyrons now skew younger than those of a current Porsche 911, driven partly by long Ferrari wait lists pushing demand into other rare modern hypercars.
* **Year of the Bugatti:** Hagerty CEO McKeel Hagerty said last year was kind of like the year of the Bugatti as newer cars become considered collectible in the market.
* **Liquidity fuels top end:** Demand is concentrated at the upper levels from company sales, IPOs and overheated stocks amid tariffs, high rates and global conflict that frets lower wealth tiers.

Domino's will launch the Domino, a[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/a1a59168-2001-486f-81ca-11ebd8a6d20f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Detroit-style pizza made for one and shaped like its logo,](https://substack.com/redirect/a1a59168-2001-486f-81ca-11ebd8a6d20f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/a1a59168-2001-486f-81ca-11ebd8a6d20f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)at stores nationwide on Aug. 31 to offer customizable personal options.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0c0039-8e17-4934-907e-bf968fe57abd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Peter, this is Mary Trump.
I just sat down with Anderson Cooper, and if you missed it, here's what I told him:
Donald and his children have always accrued their wealth by rigging the system in their favor. What troubles me most isn't the corruption itself, but how many people are still willing to look away, or even help it along.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260813-partner-mt.xFAm07&amount=5&refcode=em20260813-956&t=2&akid=956%2E34582%2EMP7DnV)
Let's be plain about what's actually happening:
**My uncle is willing to take money from virtually any foreign entity, no matter how hostile it might be to American interests. Whether it's a billion dollars from cryptocurrency or a $400 million jumbo jet from Qatar, Donald has made it clear that he's for sale, and that his personal interests come before our country's.**
We tend to forget that when Donald was indicted for stealing classified documents from the federal government, his case never went to trial because it landed before Aileen Cannon, a corrupt, loyalist judge he appointed.
None of this is new. Donald was never the self-made businessman the tabloids spent decades pretending he was. His fortune was inherited, and now his children are running the same playbook -- raking in tens of millions by leveraging the power and influence of the presidency.
**[That's exactly why people like you and me can't look away. I started Transcend PAC not to react to whatever Donald does next, but to build something durable enough to outlast this moment. Grateful to have you with me,
Mary

None of this is new. Donald was never the self-made businessman the tabloids spent decades pretending he was. His fortune was inherited, and now his children are running the same playbook -- raking in tens of millions by leveraging the power and influence of the presidency. Grateful to have you with me, Mary P.S. Peter: I'm grateful to Anderson for taking the time to speak with me. We're facing an unprecedented flood of dark money and billionaires buying their way into our politics, which makes honest journalism more important than ever. I’ll also say this: Anderson has faced years of attacks from my uncle over his sexuality. Donald has even nicknamed him "Allison Cooper." It's the same instinct that activates all of his late-night temper tantrums: attack anyone who tells the truth about him.
